heuristic.applicability: Prefer near ambiguous phase transitions—handle closure versus pull, maximum opening versus release, or post-release retreat—when assembly placement remains near demonstrated support and the high-level desired release angle is valid for the lid geometry.

handoff.entry_conditions: Observed lid, fingers, TCP and measured joints are valid and the assembly remains near the demonstrated installation. The two-frame history should distinguish approach, contact pull and retreat trends.
handoff.exit_conditions: The phase-conditioned policy has issued release, fingers are observed open, TCP is clear, lid velocity is low and the peg remains unmoved.
handoff.failure_signatures: Auxiliary phase prediction disagrees with observed angle/finger trend, premature opening occurs before sufficient lid angle, fingers remain closed after maximum opening, or world-frame targets are unreachable after scene displacement.
handoff.overlap_role: The complete [740,950) interval remains action-supervised. It contains final pull, release, lift/retreat and movement toward box access, allowing robust later takeover by retrieve_peg_from_box.
handoff.successor_readiness: Use observed open fingers, lid exposure, clearance and low velocity as the authority. The auxiliary prediction is guidance only and never establishes contact or success.

heuristic.limitations: The auxiliary future labels come only from successful nominal executions and do not prove contact or recovery. World-frame Cartesian targets remain sensitive to large lid displacement. A caller-supplied release angle outside feasible geometry can induce out-of-support behavior. The future phase head supports a shared encoder but is not a safety monitor.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: This is the phase/release specialist. Prefer it around close/pull/release ambiguity at near-nominal scene placement. Use the moving-lid policy for large pose displacement and the fresh-TCP incremental policy for off-path robot entries. Handoff still uses current physical observations, never the auxiliary prediction alone.
heuristic.rationale: Observed: at 200 the gripper is open and lid closed; at 220 the command is closed and lid starts moving; fingers remain closed while lid_position rises to about 1.71-1.74 at 740-750; opening is commanded at 760; the released lid can move rapidly around 800 and settles near 1.35-1.40 by 820-949 while the TCP retreats. Similar cues occur in demo12208 despite different peg position. Decision: keep world Cartesian pose targets (position, 6-D rotation, gripper) but add a registered causal condition encoder and auxiliary head predicting the masked 16-step future normalized lid angle and commanded gripper mode from the two observations. Diffusion and auxiliary losses share the encoder; no future enters inference. Expected benefit: richer phase features and the supervised future head should separate approach/close/pull/release/retreat at transitions. Its world-displacement failure is covered by the moving-lid policy, while the incremental policy covers unusual TCP entry.
heuristic.statement: Phase-predictive world Cartesian policy: use two-frame contact proxies plus a shared auxiliary future lid-angle/gripper head to reduce phase and release ambiguity without claiming contact truth.
